## The gap

Nothing enforces that the extras installed by `test.yml`'s sweep lanes track the extras installed
by `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` (the gating Verified lane). The two can diverge
silently, and when they do, a test can pass on the gating lane and fail on every sweep lane — or
the reverse, which is worse, because then the gate is the one that is blind.

`tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` exists to catch workflow divergence. **It was modified by
the very commit that introduced this divergence (`c57057f41`) and did not catch it.** A parity
check that does not cover the dimension that actually drifted provides confidence without
coverage.

## The concrete instance that motivated this

`c57057f41` ("Enable the grounding-terraform extra") added `--extra grounding-terraform` to
`_build-and-test.yml` and `_optionality.yml` but NOT to `test.yml`. Result, on main at
ee2c54f881d6 (run 33905162633):

- `build-and-test / pytest (macos-latest, py3.13)` — installs the extra — **PASSED**
- `sweep (declared lower-bound resolution)` — does not — **FAILED**
- `sweep (py3.14)` — does not — **FAILED**, byte-identical assertion

The proximate defect (a test missing an `importorskip` guard) is tracked separately as
`87b8-1339-383f-43f6` and is being fixed. THIS ticket is about the missing invariant that let the
two lanes drift apart unnoticed in the first place.

## Why this is worth its own ticket rather than folding into the fix

Guarding the one test makes main green. It does not stop the next extra from being added to one
workflow and not the other. The lanes have DIFFERENT and deliberate install sets — the sweep
lanes are intentionally lean, which is their whole purpose — so the invariant is NOT "the install
lines must be identical". It is something more careful: a divergence must be DELIBERATE and
VISIBLE rather than accidental.

That is a design question, which is why the acceptance criteria below do not prescribe the
mechanism.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 — A check fails when an extra is added to the gating lane's install but not to the
      sweep lanes' (or vice versa) WITHOUT an explicit, in-tree declaration that the divergence is
      intended. Prove it by introducing such a divergence and observing the check fail.
- [x] AC2 — A DELIBERATE divergence remains expressible and passes. The sweep lanes are
      intentionally leaner than the gating lane; the check must not force them to converge, or it
      will simply be disabled the first time it is inconvenient.
- [x] AC3 — The check names WHICH extra diverged and in WHICH direction, so the failure is
      actionable without reading both workflow files side by side.
- [x] AC4 — Re-running the check against `c57057f41`'s tree (the commit that introduced the real
      divergence) FAILS. This is the anti-vacuity criterion: a check that would not have caught
      the known historical instance has not been shown to work.

## Non-goals

Not changing which extras any lane installs — the current lean/gating split is deliberate and
correct. Not fixing the missing `importorskip` guard (that is `87b8-1339-383f-43f6`). Not
widening the sweep lanes.
